item.title: Week 5: Databases & Some Gentle Stats
item.description: These page draws on, re-work, and replicate portions of the Open Digital Archaeology Textbook Environment section on Databases A database is a way of systematically organizing data through carefully designed metadata schemes that describe the nature of the data - the archaeological information - as precisely as possible. Normally, we want as little ambiguity as possible so that we can count, filter, sort, or join different ‘fields’ of the data in order to discern larger patterns.
